locator: Methods, Temperature Data: hyperthermia-death sample, index sample and threshold establishment; Statistical Analysis; Figure 1.
extracted: Threshold 31.1°C was chosen using the median daily maximum on the dates of 10 hyperthermia deaths with benzoylecgonine (30.9°C, range 17.2–39.4°C) and a cumulative plot of 1382 cocaine-overdose deaths on 1096 days in 1990–1992. It was then tested on 1993–1995. The 10 heat-death dates were sampled from 1990–1995, a window that includes the test years; independence of the threshold choice from that test period is therefore not established merely by the separate 1990–1992 overdose index sample.

locator: Results, third paragraph; Figure 1 bottom panel, endpoint near 38 minutes.
extracted: Oesophageal temperature rose more during heating after cocaine than after lidocaine (P<0.001; repeated-measures analysis). The text gives no endpoint temperature difference. Editorial approximate reading of the enlarged original Figure 1: endpoint near 38 minutes, about 37.79°C with cocaine against 37.55°C with lidocaine, a difference about 0.23–0.24°C; both have SE bars. These are readings of the plot, not exact raw means or risk thresholds.

locator: Measurements, cutaneous vascular conductance definition (p.786); normalization to site maximum and Results (p.787); Results third paragraph (p.788); Figure 2 and legend (p.789).
extracted: Cutaneous vascular conductance is laser-Doppler forearm flow signal divided by mean arterial pressure, normalized to the maximum at that site; it is not flow alone. Results text at the stated highest common oesophageal temperature 37.86°C gives conductance 49±9 versus 70±5% of maximum (P=.03), and sweat rate 0.8±0.2 versus 1.0±0.1 mg/cm²/min (P=.04). Number contributing is not reported. The enlarged Figure 2's final values look about 54–55 versus 67% and about 0.86 versus 1.07 mg/cm²/min; its legend labels P<.01. The plotted endpoints differ from the text values. The legend does not identify its statistical contrast, so its P<.01 must not be assumed to test exactly the same endpoint comparison as the text's P=.03/.04. Do not substitute a reconciled analysis without underlying data. Figure 1's mean lidocaine curve also ends below 37.86°C.
